text: Some questions need more than one Cortex capability — a structured number, a search over ticket text, and a step that combines both, in an order you can't know in advance. Cortex Agents is Snowflake's managed layer for deciding which tool to call, and when, without you hand-coding the sequence.

Each run cycles through three phases: planning, where the agent reads the request and breaks a complex question into subtasks if needed; tool use, where it invokes whatever each subtask calls for; and reflection, where it evaluates what came back and decides whether it has enough to answer or needs to call another tool. That loop can repeat several times within a single request.

An agent can be configured with Cortex Analyst for structured questions grounded in a semantic view, Cortex Search for retrieval over unstructured text, a Python code-execution sandbox for ad hoc calculations, custom stored procedures or UDFs for business logic, data-to-chart for visualizing a result, and even MCP connectors or live web search when the answer isn't sitting in your warehouse at all.

Here's the shape of a minimal agent configuration: a list of tools — a Cortex Analyst text-to-SQL tool and a Cortex Search tool — plus instructions telling the agent how to behave and to cite which tool produced each fact. You call it through the agent:run REST API, and the response streams back each planning step and tool call as it happens, so a user sees progress instead of a silent wait.
Next lesson covers the piece that makes multi-turn conversations with an agent work: threads, which is the real, precise story behind "agent memory" in Cortex Agents.
